messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2026-03-14T18:10Z - region: azure-southcentral - symptom: autoscaler failing to provision GPUs, request queue growing > backlog threshold

oncall-ml: Seeing large queue on inference-prod in southcentral, latency spike for GPU jobs. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'quota exceeded' errors when trying to request new VMSS instances.

Sam L: confirming, I'm getting Azure API 403 with subscription hard limit message when creating N-series VMs. Example error: 'QuotaExceeded: The requested core quota is not available.'

Maria G: Any idea if this is per-VM SKU limit or a subscription-level core hard cap? Need to know whether we can switch SKUs or ship to another region.

Alex R: From recent runs, the autoscaler picks Standard_NC6s_v3. The error payload includes `vmFamily: "standardNCv3"` and `coresRequested: 64`. Looks like subscription cores in southcentral are exhausted.

Infra-bot: Detected repeated failures to scale: 12 attempts in 10m, last exit code 403. Triggering mitigation playbook step 1 (fallback routing).

oncall-ml: Can we fall back to smaller instances (more nodes with fewer GPUs) in same region? That would reduce per-request core count.

Sam L: We can try Standard_NC6 -> Standard_NC4 fallback, but NC4 isn't available in this cluster image set. Also our inference runtime expects 16GB VRAM; NC4 has less, may OOM for some models.

Maria G: For immediate customer impact, which workloads are affected? Support Lead: Multiple customers in higher tiers seeing elevated latency / 429s on generation endpoints; about 11 jobs queued > 30s. We have two PLG customers reporting timeouts.

Chris Ops: Starting traffic diversion to us-west2, can we tolerate additional latency for those customers? Support Lead: Yes for non-SLA customers. For dedicated customers we need to notify.

Sam L: I'll trigger the autoscaler to try alternate region routing policy for best-effort classes. Patch: set routing.policy.allowFallback=true for southcentral pool.

oncall-ml: Do that and also enable temporary batching window = 120ms to reduce per-token cost while we stabilize.

Alex R: Applying change now:
```
PATCH /config/pools/southcentral
{ "fallback_regions": ["us-west2"], "allowFallback": true }
```

Infra-bot: Config applied, autoscaler will attempt capacity in us-west2 for new requests. Existing queued requests will stay until canceled or handled by fallback.

Sam L: I've opened a support case with Azure (case 123456789) and escalated to quota team. ETA unclear, but they acknowledged a global incident affecting N-series in multiple tenants in region.

Maria G: Good. Meanwhile, can we preemptively free up cores by draining any non-critical batch jobs in southcentral?

oncall-ml: Listing active jobs and candidate cancellations: job-9871 (retrain), job-9923 (batch-embeddings), job-9940 (internal eval). I'll cancel the two batch ones.

Chris Ops: Cancellations in progress — that freed ~48 cores, but quota still below needed for the scale set Azure expects (need 64).

Support Lead: Notifying affected customers: "We've routed your requests to an alternate region; you may see slightly higher latency. We're working with the cloud provider and will update." Sending now. :email:

Sam L: Try a split strategy: provision a smaller GPU SKU in southcentral for latency-sensitive low-memory models, and route heavier models to us-west2. I'll add model-tag-based routing rule.

Alex R: Rule added: `route.modelSize <= "med" -> southcentral` else `"us-west2"`. Autoscaler will honor model placement hints.

Infra-bot: Monitor: queue depth decreased from 310 -> 78 after fallback enabled and cancellations. Token throughput recovered to 70% of baseline.

oncall-ml: Observed some 500s from clients pinned to southcentral dedicated pools. Are we able to failover dedicated capacity?

Sam L: For enterprise dedicated customers, we need explicit consent before routing out of region. Support Lead: One dedicated customer (AcmeCorp) impacted; they requested to keep in-region. Opening private channel to CS and Enterprise Sales.

Maria G: For immediate remediation path: (1) Continue fallback routing for public and PLG tiers, (2) cancel non-critical batch jobs, (3) request quota increase and escalate to Azure, (4) prepare longer-term mitigation: pre-warmed alternative SKUs and multi-region reservations.

Chris Ops: I'll coordinate with billing/finance to see if emergency quota bump via commit is viable.

Sam L: Also enabling emergency throttling rule to reject new heavy model requests with 503 rather than queue to infinity. Patch: set `maxQueueDepth=200, rejectPolicy=503` for southcentral.

Infra-bot: Policy change applied. New incoming heavy-model requests will be 503 until capacity resumes.

Support Lead: Notified customers: updated message includes link to status page and estimated 2-6 hour window pending Azure response.

Azure Support (via email, posted by Sam L): "We're investigating a regional core quota exhaustion affecting N-series. Engineers are restoring capacity, ETA unknown. We've prioritized your case."

oncall-ml: Any rollback plan if fallback causes cascading latency issues in us-west2? Alex R: We have capacity headroom in us-west2 but will monitor. If us-west2 hits <20% free capacity, we'll throttle PLG traffic again and open an emergency routing policy.

Sam L: Assigning post-incident actions:
- Alex R: implement pre-warm pool for alternate SKUs (due 3 days)
- Maria G: add enterprise runbook for consented cross-region failover (due 1 day)
- Chris Ops: escalate billing request for emergency commit (ASAP)
- oncall-ml: document exact error signatures and attach autoscaler logs to ticket (by EOD)

Support Lead: Customers alerted, CS following up with SLAs. No major data loss reported. Impact: increased latency and some 429/503 for heavy workloads for ~45 minutes peak; reduced after fallback.

Infra-bot: Incident severity downgraded to HIGH -> MEDIUM at 18:40Z after stabilization metrics met.

Sam L: Closing loop for now. Keep monitoring for 4 hours. If Azure provides quota increase before then, revert fallback.

Maria G: Thanks all. Final note: consider adding proactive quota-monitoring alert for per-SKU core exhaustion. Right now we only alert on autoscaler failure events.

Chris Ops: Noted, I'll add a metric and an alert (threshold: remaining cores < 20% for any region/SKU).

pagerbot: Incident closed from PAGE to MONITOR at 18:50Z.
